newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TOP 100 COMPANIES GLOOMY ON 1997 OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TOP 100 COMPANIES GLOOMY ON 1997 OUTLOOK.

text.p: South Africa's top 100 industrial companies are downbeat about prospects in 1997 with only 28 percent expecting an improvement in business confidence, 39 percent seeing it falling and 33 percent undecided.
That is the conclusion of the annual survey of top executives conducted by the Bureau of Market Research at the University of South Africa.

The survey showed executives expected an economic growth rate of three percent in 1997 -- better than most economists' ideas which centre around 2.0 to 2.5 percent -- and an inflation rate of about 8.8 percent.
Most independent analysts expect economic growth in 1996 to come in around three percent, down from 3.3 percent in 1995, while November consumer price inflation stood at 9.2 percent year-on-year.

Executives surveyed saw the rand falling to 5.12 on the dollar in 1997, a more bearish view than the consensus of economists polled by Reuters late last year which predicted a rand/dollar rate of 4.92 by year-end.

The vast majority of executives, 82 percent, favoured the total abolition of foreign exchange controls and 86 percent believed that the lack of a clearly defined privatisation process was a weak link in the government's economic programme.
